highlights.content: ## 1F3-OS-10a-02 *The 40th Annual Conference of the Japanese Society for Artificial Intelligence, 2026* # The Impact of Protocol Mechanics and Model Capacity on Emergent Behavior in Multilateral LLM Negotiations ### Cifong Kang<sup>∗1</sup> ### Takehisa Yairi<sup>∗1</sup> *∗*1 ### The University of Tokyo The integration of Large Language Models into Multi-Agent Systems challenges traditional game-theoretic predictions, particularly regarding the user dynamics under different voting rules. This study investigates negotiation protocols as governing mechanisms for LLM behavior, comparing high-capacity and lightweight counterparts under varying voting rules and turn-taking structures. Our results reveal a sharp divergence: lightweight models exhibit premature convergence, rushing into low-quality decisions. While rigid turn-taking exacerbates a last-mover dis- advantage for these agents, procedural stochasticity acts as a cognitive prosthetic, mitigating positional biases. Conversely, high-capacity models display alignment resilience, refusing to exploit majority rules to marginalize minorities. Instead, they consistently converge near Pareto, Nash, and Kalai-Smorodinsky optima. We attribute this to a conflict between protocol rationality and RLHF alignment biases. These findings underscore that future mechanism design must be capacity-aware, accounting for the variable cognitive constraints of AI agents. Keywords: LLM, Automated Negotiation, Multi-Agent Systems, Game Theory, Decision Making ### 1. Introduction Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have catalyzed a paradigm shift in Multi-Agent Systems (MAS), evolving these technologies from static optimization tools into autonomous agents capable of complex reasoning, social interaction, and strategic planning [Wang 24]. Negotiation and resource allocation have emerged as critical test- ing ground for this new class of agents, as they require not only linguistic fluency but also Theory of Mind (ToM) and strategic foresight [Abdelnabi 24]. However, the black box nature of LLMs introduces significant challenges for system design. While historical research in automated negotiation, such as the Automated Negotiating Agents Competition (ANAC), focused on optimiz- ing agent strategies using explicit, time-discounted heuristic functions [Baarslag 16,Kiruthika 20], this approach is insuf- ficient for LLM-based agents. Modern LLMs are not pure utility maximizers; they are heavily influenced by Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), which pri- oritizes attributes like helpfulness, harmlessness, and po- liteness [Akata 25]. We advocate for a critical shift in perspective: rather than focusing solely on agent enhancement, we examine how the negotiation protocol functions as the primary governing mechanism for emergent behavior. highlights.content: Google launched Gemini 4 Neon on November 18 — its fourth Gemini 4 model in seven weeks, priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. It debuted #1 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index with a score of 58.6, scored 61 on the AA Intelligence Index at its highest thinking setting, and reportedly matched Claude Opus 5.5 on a real coding benchmark at less than half the cost per task. > 📖 Read the full version with charts and embedded sources on ComputeLeap → Those numbers matter. But they are not the story. The story is that the leaderboard has fractured so completely that four labs can each claim #1 on a different index — and that Google is using price, not performance, as the weapon that actually moves markets. *View original announcement on Google Blog →* ## Four Models, Seven Weeks Here is what Google shipped in the Gemini 4 family since late September: | Model | Date | Role | Pricing (per 1M tokens) | |---|---|---|---| | **Gemini 4 Argon** | Sep 30 | Deep reasoning, frontier intelligence | $2 / $10 (intro) → $4 / $20 after Nov 30 | | **Gemini 4 Carbon** | Oct 28 → Nov 10 (GA) | Most complex work, cybersecurity | $2 / $10 (intro) → $4 / $20 after Nov 30 | | **Gemini 4 Hydrogen** | Nov 12 | Speed tier, cheapest frontier | $1.50 / $0.75 | | **Gemini 4 Neon** | Nov 18 | Coding agents, knowledge work | $3 / $15 | That is a new model roughly every 12 days. No other lab has matched this shipping velocity in 2026. Anthropic's last major release was Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22 — nearly two months ago. OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on November 17, the day before Neon, and the consensus across YouTube and Substack is that it "got slept on." We covered the Carbon/Hydrogen double-launch last week. The pattern continues: Google is not trying to win one benchmark cycle. It is trying to make the benchmark cycle irrelevant by shipping faster than anyone can evaluate. ## The Pricing Game The benchmarks are close enough to argue about. The pricing is not. Artificial Analysis measured the cost per Intelligence Index task across effort levels: | Model | Effort | Index Score | Cost/Task | Time/Task | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Gemini 4 Neon** | Low | 44 | $0.75 | 3.7 min | | **Gemini 4 Neon** | High (default) | 60 | $3.74 | 14.8 min | | **Gemini 4 Neon** | Xhigh | 61 | $6.44 | 21.5 min | | **Claude Opus 5.5** | Low | 35 | $0.98 | 3.0 min | | **Claude Opus 5.5** | High | 52 | $3.46 | 9.2 min | | **Claude Opus 5.5** | Max | 59 | $10.04 | 25.7 min | At the default settings that most developers actually use, Neon scores 60 at $3.74 per task. Claude Opus 5.5 scores 52 at $3.46. Neon delivers 15% more intelligence for 8% more money. At maximum effort, the gap widens — Neon hits 61 for $6.44 while Opus reaches 59 for $10.04. That is a 36% cost premium for two fewer index points. *View original article on The Neuron →* The Neuron's cost analysis puts it even more starkly: on the Coding Agent Index, Neon in Google's Antigravity CLI costs $6.86 per task versus $15.47 for Claude Fable 5.2 in Claude Code. That is 56% cheaper for a one-point advantage on the coding index (59 vs 58). > 💡 Google's pricing pattern is becoming clear: launch at an aggressive introductory rate, let developers build on it, then normalize upward. Argon and Carbon both started at $2/$10 and jump to $4/$20 on December 1. The question is whether Neon's $3/$15 is permanent or another intro hook. The cached input rate — $0.15 per million tokens, a 95% discount — is where the subsidy becomes structural. For agentic workloads that repeatedly reference the same codebase or document context, effective input costs approach zero. This is not a competitive move against Claude's pricing. highlights.content: # AI Agent Teams Recreate Human Decision Chain Reactions Research published today reveals that teams of AI agents can successfully replicate the complex chain reactions of human decision-making processes. The findings demonstrate how multi-agent systems simulate the cascading, interdependent choices that define organizational behavior, opening new pathways for modeling real-world team dynamics and risk scenarios. ## How Multi-Agent Systems Model Human Decision Cascades The research shows AI agent teams can capture the sequential nature of organizational decisions, where one person's choice triggers responses from others. Unlike single-agent models, these systems assign different agents specific roles, expertise levels, and decision-making authorities. When one agent makes a choice, others react based on their programmed constraints and objectives, mirroring how departments, managers, and frontline workers interact in actual organizations. This approach moves beyond static simulation. The agents engage in dynamic exchanges, negotiating priorities, surfacing conflicts, and adapting strategies as scenarios unfold. Early tests show the systems accurately predict decision outcomes in supply chain disruptions, budget allocation conflicts, and cross-functional project planning. ## Release Date and Availability The research was officially released on November 21, 2026, through Tech Xplore and affiliated academic channels. The underlying frameworks and methodologies are now available for academic review, with enterprise implementations expected to follow in early 2027 as organizations adapt the models for proprietary use cases. ## Applications in Organizational Risk and Planning Organizations can deploy these multi-agent decision models to test high-stakes scenarios before committing resources. Examples include: - Simulating merger integration decisions across departments with conflicting incentives - Modeling regulatory compliance responses when multiple teams interpret new rules differently - Testing product launch sequences where marketing, engineering, and finance decisions depend on each other The systems also reveal hidden dependencies. In one pilot, a retail chain discovered its inventory decisions inadvertently triggered pricing conflicts three departments downstream, a cascade invisible in traditional planning tools. ## Technical Architecture Behind Decision Replication The research employs hierarchical agent structures, where each agent maintains its own context, goals, and information access levels. Communication protocols between agents use structured message passing rather than shared memory, forcing agents to persuade, inform, or negotiate like real humans do. Some implementations incorporate reinforcement learning loops, allowing agents to adjust decision strategies based on simulated outcomes over multiple iterations. Researchers noted the importance of asymmetric information distribution. Agents don't see the full picture simultaneously, they receive updates at different times and with varying detail levels, replicating the information fragmentation common in large organizations. ## What This Means This capability transforms how organizations approach scenario planning and risk management. Instead of relying on static spreadsheets or intuition, decision-makers can run realistic simulations where AI agents embody different stakeholder perspectives and constraints. The technology also advances collaborative AI design, proving that agent teams can handle the messy, interdependent logic of human organizational life. As these models mature, expect them to become standard tools for strategic planning, change management, and enterprise AI deployment where multiple autonomous systems must coordinate decisions without centralized control. on Emergent today

highlights.titleZh: Apple plans autonomous AI agent to take on OpenAI and Meta, but could its iPhone ecosystem give it an edge? | Mint
highlights.content: Apple could be preparing a bigger move in Artificial Intelligence (AI) as it looks to catch up with rivals such an OpenAI, Meta, Google, and Anthropic. The company is reportedly developing an autonomous AI agent that can carry out several tasks across apps, websites, and devices without users having to guide through every step. The development came to light through Apple's recent job listings, which describe plans for an AI system that can browse the internet, control applications, write and debug code, and use different services to complete tasks. The move could mark an important change in Apple's AI strategy. While competitors have already started offering AI tools that can do more than answer questions, Apple is now looking to build a system that can take action on behalf of the users. According to a report by Bloomberg, one of Apple's job listings seeks a senior engineering manager for its Agentc AI team. The listing describes an AI agent that can use a computer like a person, choosing the right tools to complete different tasks. The original listing was later removed from Apple's careers website, but its details have been reported by several technology publications. Unlike a regular chatbot an autonomous AI agent is designed to complete tasks rather than simply respond to questions. Users can give it a goal, and the system can work around the steps needed to achieve it. For example, instead of asking Siri how to find information across different apps, a user could potentially ask an AI agent to collect information from websites, organise it and prepare a result. The agent would then handle the different steps involved. Apple's job description also refers to the use of specialised sub-agents. This means the main AI system could divide a complicated task into smaller parts and assign them to different AI systems before bringing the results together. The company is also looking at how these agents can work across browsers, applications, command lines and software services. This suggests Apple wants to build something more capable than a traditional voice assistant. The effort appears to involve teams working on Siri, Apple's user interface systems and its own AI models. A separate Apple job listing for an Applied AI Engineer working on the Siri agent platform also talks about building systems that can plan tasks, use tools and work with models running both on devices and through Apple's Private Cloud Compute infrastructure Apple has not announced a finished product or shared a launch date for the proposed agent. Its job listings reveal the direction of its work, but they do not confirm when users will get access to these features. Apple may have an advantage that some of its competitors do not have to the same extent: its connected ecosystem of devices and services. The company has a large number of users who already rely on iPhones, Macs, iPads and Apple Watches. If its AI agent can work smoothly across these devices, Apple could make it easier for people to use AI as part of their everyday activities. Privacy could also play an important role. Apple has repeatedly presented privacy as a key part of its AI plans. Its job listings describe an agent that should work privately, with safety and security built into its design. Apple has already been working on a more capable version of Siri. In June 2026, the company announced its next-generation Siri experience, with features including personal context understanding, on-screen awareness and the ability to take more actions across apps. highlights.content: # Nvidia Earnings Beat Triggers 14% Stock Plunge in 2026 **Officially launched on November 21, 2026.** Nvidia reported third-quarter 2026 earnings that exceeded analyst expectations on November 21, 2026, yet the semiconductor giant's shares plummeted 14% in a dramatic market response that underscores growing investor skepticism about AI infrastructure spending. The earnings beat, which would typically trigger rallies, instead accelerated the company's longest weekly losing streak since the 2008 financial crisis, wiping out roughly $2.6 trillion in market value across seven consecutive weeks of declines. ## Earnings Performance Versus Market Reaction Nvidia's Q3 2026 results showed continued strength in data center revenue, with the company's AI accelerator chips maintaining dominant market share in generative AI workloads. Revenue figures surpassed Wall Street consensus estimates by approximately 8%, while adjusted earnings per share beat projections by double digits. The company's data center segment, which accounts for over 80% of total revenue, posted year-over-year growth exceeding 40% despite macroeconomic headwinds. However, investors focused on forward guidance that suggested decelerating growth rates in coming quarters. Management commentary acknowledged extended sales cycles for enterprise AI deployments and raised concerns about chip supply constraints that could limit revenue upside through mid-2027. These cautious notes overshadowed the strong quarterly performance, triggering the sharp sell-off. ## Seven-Week Decline Context The 14% single-day drop compounds Nvidia's worst sustained decline in nearly two decades. Since early October 2026, the stock has shed over $2.6 trillion in market capitalization as investor sentiment shifted from euphoria over AI infrastructure buildout to skepticism about return-on-investment timelines for major cloud providers and enterprise customers. Analysts point to three key factors driving the prolonged weakness: rising competition from custom AI chips developed by hyperscalers, concerns about overbuilding in data center capacity, and valuation compression across the broader technology sector. The seven-week losing streak marks the first time since 2008 that Nvidia has experienced such extended downward momentum, raising questions about whether the AI chip supercycle has reached a maturation phase. Some institutional investors are rotating out of semiconductor positions into direct AI application providers, viewing the value chain's profit concentration as shifting downstream. ## Industry Implications for AI Infrastructure Nvidia's stock performance carries significant implications for the broader AI ecosystem. The company's chips power the majority of large language model training and inference workloads, making its financial health a barometer for AI sector investment appetite. The muted reaction to strong earnings suggests investors are demanding higher proof points that generative AI applications can generate sufficient revenue to justify the hundreds of billions in infrastructure spending committed by major technology companies. Competing chip architectures from AMD, custom silicon from cloud providers, and emerging startups targeting specialized AI workloads are fragmenting what was previously Nvidia's near-monopoly market position. This competitive pressure, combined with lengthening enterprise sales cycles, creates uncertainty about Nvidia's ability to maintain its historically high gross margins and revenue growth rates through 2027 and beyond. ## What This Means Nvidia's earnings-day collapse reflects a fundamental reassessment of AI infrastructure economics rather than weakness in the company's operational execution. highlights.content: # Prediction: Nvidia Stock Will Be Worth This Much in 1 Year Nvidia's business still looks rock-solid despite the company's recent challenges. ByAnthony Di Pizio – ## Key Points - Nvidia founder Jensen Huang made a shock exit from the company on Nov. 12, casting a cloud of uncertainty over the future. - Nevertheless, Nvidia just reported another blockbuster set of quarterly results, complete with an increase in forward sales guidance. - Nvidia stock is currently down 37% from its all-time high, but I think it will recover over the next 12 months. On Nov. 12, **Nvidia** (NVDA -14.01%) founder and chief executive officer Jensen Huang resigned from his post after a series of extramarital affairs (including one with an alleged Chinese spy) came to light. To make matters worse, the U.S. government is now investigating some of the company's customers in Southeast Asia to determine whether advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips were illegally forwarded to businesses in China. Nvidia stock has plummeted by 37% from its peak amid the turmoil, and it's now trading at the cheapest valuation in a decade. However, the company just reported a blockbuster set of operating results for its fiscal 2027 third quarter (ended Oct. 25), and interim CEO Colette Kress even issued a higher revenue forecast for the upcoming 2028 fiscal year. As a result, while Nvidia's challenges are likely to cause further short-term volatility in its stock, I think its booming business and solid fundamentals will ultimately prevail. Here's where I predict the stock will be trading in one year. Image source: Nvidia. ## The Vera Rubin launch has been a resounding success Nvidia has come a long way since launching its first dedicated AI graphics processing unit (GPU) for the data center, the Hopper-based H100, in 2022. It went on to release the Blackwell and Blackwell Ultra architectures in 2024 and 2025, the latter of which can deliver up to 50 times more output performance than Hopper. But Nvidia started shipping its new Vera Rubin systems during the recent third quarter, which include the Rubin GPU, Vera central processing unit (CPU), and a series of upgraded networking components. It can deliver up to 30 times the performance of the equivalent Blackwell Ultra system, translating into a potential 97% reduction in inference token costs. Inference tokens are the text, images, or computer code generated by an AI model in response to a prompt, so Vera Rubin could significantly reduce the cost of running AI software. This is likely to drive greater AI adoption while making data center operators more profitable, fueling further demand for Nvidia's chips. Colette Kress said Vera Rubin achieved almost $20 billion in sales during the third quarter alone, making this the fastest product ramp in Nvidia's history. ## NVDA - Nvidia NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26 ## Nvidia's third-quarter revenue doubled Nvidia generated a record $115.8 billion in revenue during the third quarter, a whopping 103% increase from the year-ago period. The data center segment alone accounted for $107.6 billion of that total, and it grew at an even faster pace of 110%. Nvidia's physical AI business also deserves a mention. It develops the hardware and software technologies required to run robots, autonomous vehicles, industrial systems, and more, and its revenue more than *tripled* year over year during the third quarter. It's now on track to generate $25 billion in total sales for the current fiscal year (which ends on Jan. 31, 2027), so it could soon become a key source of growth for the entire company. Kress also said Nvidia could deliver $130 billion in total revenue during the fourth quarter, exceeding Wall Street's consensus expectation of $125.1 billion. highlights.content: ## Key Takeaways Grammarly CEO Shishir Mehrotra explains Superhuman Go, an agent platform riding Grammarly's in-app presence and sub-100ms inference to close AI's "last mile," arguing agents must reach users at the cursor rather than add detours. ## Summary Shishir Mehrotra, CEO of Superhuman, argues that the biggest gap in enterprise AI is not model capability but the "last mile" — getting AI to the point where people already work, rather than requiring them to change behavior and go to a separate tool. He makes the case during a product-launch interview covering Superhuman Go (an agent platform built on Grammarly), a new personal-assistant capability, and updates across Superhuman Mail, Superhuman Docs, and the recently acquired note-taker Fathom. The conversation spends most of its time on that last-mile thesis, Grammarly's scale and custom-inference economics, and how to measure AI productivity; the headline figure of 100 billion weekly LLM calls is one data point inside that discussion rather than its subject. Mehrotra is well placed to make the argument: Grammarly is the base product of the Superhuman suite, and he also sits on the boards of Walmart and Spotify, where he says AI productivity is now a standing topic. The reader should come away with the specific numbers behind Grammarly's inference stack, the product-by-product logic of the suite, and the open question the episode leaves unresolved — that nobody, including the guest, has a settled way to measure whether AI is actually making work better. ## The last mile, not the model, is where AI value leaks Mehrotra's central claim is that powerful AI tools fail to reach users because they demand a behavior change: you have to remember to open them, formulate the right query, and fold them into your day. He calls this "the last mile of AI." Grammarly's counter-model is to bring AI to the cursor inside whatever application the user is already in. The strategic bet behind Superhuman Go is to pair the two — the powerful standalone tools with Grammarly's distribution into the workflow. He illustrates with a legal example. Lora, a partner product, is described as a ChatGPT-like tool infused with global and company-specific legal knowledge. But it is "optimized for the case where the lawyer remembers to go to it," and Mehrotra says his own in-house lawyers use such tools "once or twice a week" at most. Move that same capability to the cursor — while reviewing a contract, drafting a client email, or taking meeting notes — and it can flag a clause the company won't accept or reframe a term in real time. His claim: bringing existing AI to the cursor can "100x the usage of your AI tools." > "The challenge we think is the last mile of AI. These tools all require you to have a massive change in behavior. You have to remember to go to them." ## Grammarly's scale rests on custom models at sub-100ms latency The numbers Mehrotra cites are the most concrete in the episode and frame Grammarly as an inference business, not just a writing assistant. By his account, Grammarly handles over 100 billion LLM calls per week — more than 2,000 per user per day — and serves 98% of them from its own custom models at under 100 milliseconds of latency. He says this makes Grammarly the most-used AI product for most of its users. | Metric | Figure (per Mehrotra) | |---|---| | Weekly LLM calls | Over 100 billion | | Calls per user per day | Over 2,000 | | Share served by custom models | 98% | | Latency on custom models | Under 100 ms | | Unique applications Grammarly works in | 1 million per day | The 1-million-application figure is the distribution asset. Grammarly observes what the user is doing across desktop, web, and mobile apps, annotates unobtrusively, and makes changes on the user's behalf. Mehrotra calls that ability "a missing ingredient" not just for Grammarly but for any product trying to deliver AI where users work. AI Agents.content: ### AI Agents Directory Daily Brief: November 21, 2026 The AI landscape saw significant financial and developmental milestones this week. Anthropic has reportedly priced its IPO at a staggering $81.3 billion, marking a major event in the AI sector. In parallel, the startup LATO secured $4.7 million in seed funding to develop AI agents for conducting due diligence interviews for investors. Everful also raised $48.5 million for AI agents designed to source and vet products for small retailers. Big tech continues its push into AI agent development. Apple is reportedly building its own AI agent, with job listings revealing plans for an agent capable of controlling devices, managing applications, browsing the web, and coding. This move positions Apple to rival existing AI agents from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta. Meanwhile, Google's Gemini API introduced Tool Retrieval, allowing agents to load tool parameters only when needed, optimizing performance. The capabilities of AI agents are expanding, with new tools emerging to automate tasks and build applications. Claude AI has demonstrated autonomous software development by building a Rust web browser from scratch. Discussions also highlight advancements in multi-agent workflows and techniques for building more complex, self-correcting AI agents using frameworks like LangGraph. The potential for these agents to become a new form of tech monopoly is also a growing concern. #### Source-linked headlines Anthropic has priced its Initial Public Offering at $81.3 billion. This significant valuation underscores the immense financial interest in the artificial intelligence sector. Why it matters: This IPO represents a major financial milestone for an AI company and signals strong investor confidence in the future of AI. LATO has secured $4.7 million in seed funding, co-led by Air Street Capital and Axiom Partners. The company will use the funds to develop AI agents for conducting customer and expert interviews for private equity. Why it matters: This funding highlights the growing application of AI agents in specialized financial due diligence processes. Everful has raised $48.5 million to develop AI agents focused on sourcing products. These agents will vet factories and manage shipping for small retailers with low minimum orders. Why it matters: This investment supports the expansion of AI agents into e-commerce logistics and supply chain management for smaller businesses.

AI Agents.content: ## 1F3-OS-10a-02 *The 40th Annual Conference of the Japanese Society for Artificial Intelligence, 2026* # The Impact of Protocol Mechanics and Model Capacity on Emergent Behavior in Multilateral LLM Negotiations ### Cifong Kang<sup>∗1</sup> ### Takehisa Yairi<sup>∗1</sup> *∗*1 ### The University of Tokyo The integration of Large Language Models into Multi-Agent Systems challenges traditional game-theoretic predictions, particularly regarding the user dynamics under different voting rules. This study investigates negotiation protocols as governing mechanisms for LLM behavior, comparing high-capacity and lightweight counterparts under varying voting rules and turn-taking structures. Our results reveal a sharp divergence: lightweight models exhibit premature convergence, rushing into low-quality decisions. While rigid turn-taking exacerbates a last-mover dis- advantage for these agents, procedural stochasticity acts as a cognitive prosthetic, mitigating positional biases. Conversely, high-capacity models display alignment resilience, refusing to exploit majority rules to marginalize minorities. Instead, they consistently converge near Pareto, Nash, and Kalai-Smorodinsky optima. We attribute this to a conflict between protocol rationality and RLHF alignment biases. These findings underscore that future mechanism design must be capacity-aware, accounting for the variable cognitive constraints of AI agents. Keywords: LLM, Automated Negotiation, Multi-Agent Systems, Game Theory, Decision Making ### 1. Introduction Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have catalyzed a paradigm shift in Multi-Agent Systems (MAS), evolving these technologies from static optimization tools into autonomous agents capable of complex reasoning, social interaction, and strategic planning [Wang 24]. Negotiation and resource allocation have emerged as critical test- ing ground for this new class of agents, as they require not only linguistic fluency but also Theory of Mind (ToM) and strategic foresight [Abdelnabi 24]. However, the black box nature of LLMs introduces significant challenges for system design. While historical research in automated negotiation, such as the Automated Negotiating Agents Competition (ANAC), focused on optimiz- ing agent strategies using explicit, time-discounted heuristic functions [Baarslag 16,Kiruthika 20], this approach is insuf- ficient for LLM-based agents. Modern LLMs are not pure utility maximizers; they are heavily influenced by Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), which pri- oritizes attributes like helpfulness, harmlessness, and po- liteness [Akata 25]. We advocate for a critical shift in perspective: rather than focusing solely on agent enhancement, we examine how the negotiation protocol functions as the primary governing mechanism for emergent behavior. [Zhou 24, Aydo˘gan 17] This research investigates the tension between strict game-theoretic structures and the ingrained behavioral biases of safety-aligned LLMs In multilateral negotiations, cooperative game theory dis- tinguishes between unanimity, where veto power serves to enforce fairness, and majority rule, which inherently in- centivizes exclusionary coalitions [Beersma 02, Ten Velden 07]. Leveraging the Stacked Alternating Offers Protocol (SAOP) [Aydo˘gan 17], we manipulate protocol mechanics to establish two key insights. AI Agents.content: # AI Agent Teams Recreate Human Decision Chain Reactions Research published today reveals that teams of AI agents can successfully replicate the complex chain reactions of human decision-making processes. The findings demonstrate how multi-agent systems simulate the cascading, interdependent choices that define organizational behavior, opening new pathways for modeling real-world team dynamics and risk scenarios. ## How Multi-Agent Systems Model Human Decision Cascades The research shows AI agent teams can capture the sequential nature of organizational decisions, where one person's choice triggers responses from others. Unlike single-agent models, these systems assign different agents specific roles, expertise levels, and decision-making authorities. When one agent makes a choice, others react based on their programmed constraints and objectives, mirroring how departments, managers, and frontline workers interact in actual organizations. This approach moves beyond static simulation. The agents engage in dynamic exchanges, negotiating priorities, surfacing conflicts, and adapting strategies as scenarios unfold. Early tests show the systems accurately predict decision outcomes in supply chain disruptions, budget allocation conflicts, and cross-functional project planning. ## Release Date and Availability The research was officially released on November 21, 2026, through Tech Xplore and affiliated academic channels. The underlying frameworks and methodologies are now available for academic review, with enterprise implementations expected to follow in early 2027 as organizations adapt the models for proprietary use cases. ## Applications in Organizational Risk and Planning Organizations can deploy these multi-agent decision models to test high-stakes scenarios before committing resources. Examples include: - Simulating merger integration decisions across departments with conflicting incentives - Modeling regulatory compliance responses when multiple teams interpret new rules differently - Testing product launch sequences where marketing, engineering, and finance decisions depend on each other The systems also reveal hidden dependencies. In one pilot, a retail chain discovered its inventory decisions inadvertently triggered pricing conflicts three departments downstream, a cascade invisible in traditional planning tools. ## Technical Architecture Behind Decision Replication The research employs hierarchical agent structures, where each agent maintains its own context, goals, and information access levels. Communication protocols between agents use structured message passing rather than shared memory, forcing agents to persuade, inform, or negotiate like real humans do. Some implementations incorporate reinforcement learning loops, allowing agents to adjust decision strategies based on simulated outcomes over multiple iterations. Researchers noted the importance of asymmetric information distribution. Agents don't see the full picture simultaneously, they receive updates at different times and with varying detail levels, replicating the information fragmentation common in large organizations. ## What This Means This capability transforms how organizations approach scenario planning and risk management. Instead of relying on static spreadsheets or intuition, decision-makers can run realistic simulations where AI agents embody different stakeholder perspectives and constraints. The technology also advances collaborative AI design, proving that agent teams can handle the messy, interdependent logic of human organizational life. AI Agents.titleZh: Apple plans autonomous AI agent to take on OpenAI and Meta, but could its iPhone ecosystem give it an edge? | Mint
AI Agents.content: Apple could be preparing a bigger move in Artificial Intelligence (AI) as it looks to catch up with rivals such an OpenAI, Meta, Google, and Anthropic. The company is reportedly developing an autonomous AI agent that can carry out several tasks across apps, websites, and devices without users having to guide through every step. The development came to light through Apple's recent job listings, which describe plans for an AI system that can browse the internet, control applications, write and debug code, and use different services to complete tasks. The move could mark an important change in Apple's AI strategy. While competitors have already started offering AI tools that can do more than answer questions, Apple is now looking to build a system that can take action on behalf of the users. According to a report by Bloomberg, one of Apple's job listings seeks a senior engineering manager for its Agentc AI team. The listing describes an AI agent that can use a computer like a person, choosing the right tools to complete different tasks. The original listing was later removed from Apple's careers website, but its details have been reported by several technology publications. Unlike a regular chatbot an autonomous AI agent is designed to complete tasks rather than simply respond to questions. Users can give it a goal, and the system can work around the steps needed to achieve it. For example, instead of asking Siri how to find information across different apps, a user could potentially ask an AI agent to collect information from websites, organise it and prepare a result. The agent would then handle the different steps involved. Apple's job description also refers to the use of specialised sub-agents. This means the main AI system could divide a complicated task into smaller parts and assign them to different AI systems before bringing the results together. The company is also looking at how these agents can work across browsers, applications, command lines and software services. This suggests Apple wants to build something more capable than a traditional voice assistant. The effort appears to involve teams working on Siri, Apple's user interface systems and its own AI models. A separate Apple job listing for an Applied AI Engineer working on the Siri agent platform also talks about building systems that can plan tasks, use tools and work with models running both on devices and through Apple's Private Cloud Compute infrastructure Apple has not announced a finished product or shared a launch date for the proposed agent. Its job listings reveal the direction of its work, but they do not confirm when users will get access to these features. Apple may have an advantage that some of its competitors do not have to the same extent: its connected ecosystem of devices and services. The company has a large number of users who already rely on iPhones, Macs, iPads and Apple Watches. If its AI agent can work smoothly across these devices, Apple could make it easier for people to use AI as part of their everyday activities. Privacy could also play an important role. Apple has repeatedly presented privacy as a key part of its AI plans. Its job listings describe an agent that should work privately, with safety and security built into its design. Apple has already been working on a more capable version of Siri. In June 2026, the company announced its next-generation Siri experience, with features including personal context understanding, on-screen awareness and the ability to take more actions across apps. All of this work is done in collaboration with human experts, and we are making these tools available externally. ## Quick links * [Antigravity blog](https://antigravity.google/blog/gemini-4-argon-trillion-edge-graphs-and-tpu-kernels) * [Gemini 4 Argon](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-argon/) * [Antigravity Teamwork](https://antigravity.google/blog/teamwork-when-ai-becomes-a-research-partner) * [Researcher access program](https://forms.gle/WvmBbPvRbpKG1BPn9) * + × Over the past several weeks, teams across Google and academic partner institutions have tackled open problems in math, science, and complex systems engineering that had remained open for years. Using [Gemini 4 Argon](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-argon/), [Gemini 4 Carbon](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-4-carbon-now-available/), [Gemini 4 Hydrogen](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-hydrogen/) and multi-agent workflows such as [Antigravity’s /teamwork](https://antigravity.google/blog/teamwork-when-ai-becomes-a-research-partner) (building on various Gemini models), these collaborations have produced new innovations across information theory, formal verifications, molecular structure discoveries, and kernel optimization, along with several production infrastructure gains at Google. We are making these agentic tools available in Antigravity’s /teamwork (alongside [/boost](https://antigravity.google/docs/boost) and other agents) so that researchers and developers can apply them to their own work. Frontier research and systems engineering require navigating vast literature, building custom computational pipelines, testing against physical measurements, and verifying every step. Progress comes from an interactive discovery loop where researchers frame questions and define the theoretical or physical constraints, while long-horizon agents write custom solvers, explore large search spaces, test candidate designs, and check long chains of logic. ## Scaling long-horizon reasoning Two limits of current language models motivate [/teamwork's design](https://antigravity.google/blog/teamwork-when-ai-becomes-a-research-partner/). First, model generation can be unpredictable, leaving a gap between a single attempt and finding the correct answer. The system bridges this gap by pairing parallel exploration with dedicated falsifiers (e.g., the [Lean 4](https://lean-lang.org/) proof checker, unmodified software test suites, execution simulators, web search, or hardware counters) to automatically verify which candidate solutions work. Second, AI models often lose track of details over multi-day tasks because attention disperses across growing context windows. To prevent this, /teamwork partitions context by construction: each specialized agent receives only the exact files and tools it needs for a specific step. Coordinators hand off tasks to fresh successors, while critics and auditors challenge and verify results from clean contexts without the original producer's reasoning. Teamwork expresses these workflows as declarative self-improving natural-language patterns and dynamically routes each user prompt to the pattern best suited to the task. AI Agents.content: Artificial intelligence continues to transform scientific research, financial markets, software development, and global technology competition. On November 21, 2026, five important developments are attracting attention across the AI industry: Anthropic’s reported mathematical breakthrough with Claude, its record-breaking stock market debut, Google’s new Gemini computer-use capabilities for Mac, growing US restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI chips, and President Donald Trump’s proposal to penalize American companies building AI data centers overseas. These developments highlight how quickly artificial intelligence is moving beyond chatbots and content generation. AI systems are increasingly becoming research partners, workplace assistants, economic assets, and strategic infrastructure. In this edition of AI News Today, we examine the five biggest developments, explain why they matter, and explore what they could mean for businesses, developers, investors, and the future of artificial intelligence. ## 1. Anthropic Researcher Claims Claude Helped Prove the Riemann Hypothesis One of the most remarkable AI research stories this week comes from Anthropic, the company behind Claude AI. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge has announced that he believes he has discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis while working with Claude. The Riemann Hypothesis is a famous mathematical problem first proposed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859. It concerns the distribution of prime numbers and has remained one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics. The announcement is attracting international attention because the problem has challenged mathematicians for more than 160 years. ### How Did Claude Contribute? According to Alpöge’s announcement, Claude assisted in developing the mathematical approach behind the proposed proof. The researcher released a four-page document outlining the claimed result. However, there is an important distinction between a proposed proof and a mathematically established solution. The document has not yet undergone independent expert verification. Mathematicians have also raised questions about the clarity and completeness of the published explanation. The Clay Mathematics Institute lists the Riemann Hypothesis among its Millennium Prize Problems, with a $1 million prize attached to an accepted solution. Therefore, the hypothesis should not yet be described as officially solved. ### Why This AI Development Matters If the proposed proof survives independent mathematical review, it could represent a major milestone in AI-assisted scientific research. The development also demonstrates a potentially important role for advanced language models: helping researchers explore complex problems, test ideas, and develop mathematical arguments. However, AI-generated reasoning still requires human expertise, verification, and rigorous scientific review. **Industry takeaway:** Claude’s involvement in this research could strengthen the case for AI as a scientific research assistant, but the mathematical claim remains unverified. Source: Nature – https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03812-7 Additional reporting: AFP – https://www.afp.com/en/anthropic-researcher-says-claude-solved-maths-greatest-riddle ## 2. Anthropic’s Record-Breaking IPO Raises $81 Billion as Shares Face Early Pressure Anthropic has also attracted major attention in financial markets following its historic initial public offering (IPO). LLMs.content: Google launched Gemini 4 Neon on November 18 — its fourth Gemini 4 model in seven weeks, priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. But they are not the story. The story is that the leaderboard has fractured so completely that four labs can each claim #1 on a different index — and that Google is using price, not performance, as the weapon that actually moves markets. *View original announcement on Google Blog →* ## Four Models, Seven Weeks Here is what Google shipped in the Gemini 4 family since late September: | Model | Date | Role | Pricing (per 1M tokens) | |---|---|---|---| | **Gemini 4 Argon** | Sep 30 | Deep reasoning, frontier intelligence | $2 / $10 (intro) → $4 / $20 after Nov 30 | | **Gemini 4 Carbon** | Oct 28 → Nov 10 (GA) | Most complex work, cybersecurity | $2 / $10 (intro) → $4 / $20 after Nov 30 | | **Gemini 4 Hydrogen** | Nov 12 | Speed tier, cheapest frontier | $1.50 / $0.75 | | **Gemini 4 Neon** | Nov 18 | Coding agents, knowledge work | $3 / $15 | That is a new model roughly every 12 days. No other lab has matched this shipping velocity in 2026. Anthropic's last major release was Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22 — nearly two months ago. OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on November 17, the day before Neon, and the consensus across YouTube and Substack is that it "got slept on." We covered the Carbon/Hydrogen double-launch last week. The pattern continues: Google is not trying to win one benchmark cycle. He makes the case during a product-launch interview covering Superhuman Go (an agent platform built on Grammarly), a new personal-assistant capability, and updates across Superhuman Mail, Superhuman Docs, and the recently acquired note-taker Fathom. The conversation spends most of its time on that last-mile thesis, Grammarly's scale and custom-inference economics, and how to measure AI productivity; the headline figure of 100 billion weekly LLM calls is one data point inside that discussion rather than its subject. Mehrotra is well placed to make the argument: Grammarly is the base product of the Superhuman suite, and he also sits on the boards of Walmart and Spotify, where he says AI productivity is now a standing topic. The reader should come away with the specific numbers behind Grammarly's inference stack, the product-by-product logic of the suite, and the open question the episode leaves unresolved — that nobody, including the guest, has a settled way to measure whether AI is actually making work better. ## The last mile, not the model, is where AI value leaks Mehrotra's central claim is that powerful AI tools fail to reach users because they demand a behavior change: you have to remember to open them, formulate the right query, and fold them into your day. He calls this "the last mile of AI." Grammarly's counter-model is to bring AI to the cursor inside whatever application the user is already in. The strategic bet behind Superhuman Go is to pair the two — the powerful standalone tools with Grammarly's distribution into the workflow. He illustrates with a legal example. Lora, a partner product, is described as a ChatGPT-like tool infused with global and company-specific legal knowledge. But it is "optimized for the case where the lawyer remembers to go to it," and Mehrotra says his own in-house lawyers use such tools "once or twice a week" at most. Move that same capability to the cursor — while reviewing a contract, drafting a client email, or taking meeting notes — and it can flag a clause the company won't accept or reframe a term in real time. His claim: bringing existing AI to the cursor can "100x the usage of your AI tools." > "The challenge we think is the last mile of AI. These tools all require you to have a massive change in behavior. You have to remember to go to them." ## Grammarly's scale rests on custom models at sub-100ms latency The numbers Mehrotra cites are the most concrete in the episode and frame Grammarly as an inference business, not just a writing assistant. AI Product.content: A 13-year-old student from Hyderabad has launched **KIKA AI**, an artificial intelligence platform designed to help school students and young creators build projects using multiple AI agents and models through a single interface. Kiyan, a Class 9 student at Delhi Public School, Hyderabad, founded the platform after finding conventional developer tools too technically complex. Instead of navigating complicated setups, he wanted to create a simpler environment where users could focus on building projects and using AI. The platform has also received seed funding from Tasleem Arif, a technology leader with more than two decades of experience in the smartphone, software and embedded systems industries. ## KIKA AI: How the idea took shape Kiyan started developing KIKA AI on July 13, 2026. The platform reached a working product in approximately 11 weeks. The idea emerged from his own experience of working with developer tools. He found that technical requirements and complex configurations could make it difficult for beginners to turn their ideas into working projects. KIKA AI was developed to address this challenge by bringing different AI agents and models together in one place. The platform aims to reduce the technical barriers that students and young creators often encounter when experimenting with artificial intelligence. ## Features and target audience KIKA AI describes itself as an AI-native platform, with a unified interface that allows users to access multiple AI agents and models. Its primary audience includes school students, particularly those interested in using artificial intelligence for projects and creative work without having to navigate conventional developer environments. The platform’s broader objective is to make AI tools more accessible to students across India. According to figures cited at the launch, India has approximately 9 crore students studying in Classes 8 to 12. This represents nearly 6% of the country’s population and forms the potential audience KIKA AI hopes to reach. ## KIKA AI receives seed funding KIKA AI has received seed funding from Tasleem Arif, who has spent more than two decades working across the smartphone, software and embedded systems industries. Commenting on Kiyan’s initiative, Arif said the young founder demonstrated the ability to identify a real problem and work towards developing a solution. Prashant Singh, CEO of ONGC Green Limited, also praised the initiative, describing it as “truly inspiring”. The funding provides early support for the student-led venture as it works towards its goal of making artificial intelligence easier to use for younger audiences. ## What is next for the student-led AI venture? KIKA AI enters the market with a focus on school students at a time when artificial intelligence tools are increasingly being used for learning and academic projects. However, the platform has not yet disclosed its pricing structure or the number of users it has onboarded. Further details about its commercial model and user adoption remain unavailable. Meanwhile, Kiyan continues to pursue his Class 9 studies alongside developing the platform, balancing his academic responsibilities with building an AI-focused venture. **Also Read:** Bengaluru Entrepreneur Turns ₹5 Lakh Investment Into ₹20 Lakh Bindi Business

Feed the AI your rough, bulleted notes on an employee's achievements and areas for improvement over the quarter. Ask it to draft a structured review. You still do the actual managing, coaching, and editing, but the AI breaks the blank-page paralysis. 3. Afterwards, use this prompt: "Give me the top 3 risks identified in this meeting and the timeline we agreed upon." It now comes in **five sizes**, E2B, E4B, 12B, 26B A4B and 31B, and every one of them reads text and images and writes text. You download the weights once and run them on your own phone, laptop or server, with no subscription and no internet connection. The hard part is not getting Gemma 4. The hard part is picking the size your machine can actually hold. The names hide the memory bill. The “4B active” 26B model still needs room for all 26 billion parameters. This guide maps each Gemma 4 model to the Mac that runs it, using Google’s own memory figures. It then covers three ways to install it, its scores, how it stacks up against Qwen 3.6, and what it cannot do. ## The Key Takeaways > * **Five sizes, all free:** E2B, E4B, 12B, 26B A4B and 31B, under **Apache 2.0**, which allows commercial use. > * **Memory decides the model:** at 4-bit, Google lists **2.9GB** for E2B, **6.7GB** for the 12B and **17.5GB** for the 31B, before any context. > * **The Mac short version:** 8GB runs E2B, 16GB runs E4B or the 12B, the 26B A4B wants **24GB or more**, and the 31B is happiest at **32GB+**. > * **Strong for its size, not a frontier model:** the 31B scores **84.3%** on GPQA Diamond, but Alibaba’s own table puts Qwen3.6-27B ahead on coding, **77.2% vs 52.0%** on SWE-bench Verified. > * **Reads, does not draw:** Gemma 4 takes images (and audio on the small models) as input but only writes text, and its training data stops in **January 2025**. ## What Is Gemma 4? Infra & Chips.content: # Nvidia Earnings Beat Triggers 14% Stock Plunge in 2026 **Officially launched on November 21, 2026.** Nvidia reported third-quarter 2026 earnings that exceeded analyst expectations on November 21, 2026, yet the semiconductor giant's shares plummeted 14% in a dramatic market response that underscores growing investor skepticism about AI infrastructure spending. The earnings beat, which would typically trigger rallies, instead accelerated the company's longest weekly losing streak since the 2008 financial crisis, wiping out roughly $2.6 trillion in market value across seven consecutive weeks of declines. ## Earnings Performance Versus Market Reaction Nvidia's Q3 2026 results showed continued strength in data center revenue, with the company's AI accelerator chips maintaining dominant market share in generative AI workloads. Revenue figures surpassed Wall Street consensus estimates by approximately 8%, while adjusted earnings per share beat projections by double digits. The company's data center segment, which accounts for over 80% of total revenue, posted year-over-year growth exceeding 40% despite macroeconomic headwinds. However, investors focused on forward guidance that suggested decelerating growth rates in coming quarters. Management commentary acknowledged extended sales cycles for enterprise AI deployments and raised concerns about chip supply constraints that could limit revenue upside through mid-2027. These cautious notes overshadowed the strong quarterly performance, triggering the sharp sell-off. ## Seven-Week Decline Context The 14% single-day drop compounds Nvidia's worst sustained decline in nearly two decades. Since early October 2026, the stock has shed over $2.6 trillion in market capitalization as investor sentiment shifted from euphoria over AI infrastructure buildout to skepticism about return-on-investment timelines for major cloud providers and enterprise customers. Analysts point to three key factors driving the prolonged weakness: rising competition from custom AI chips developed by hyperscalers, concerns about overbuilding in data center capacity, and valuation compression across the broader technology sector. The seven-week losing streak marks the first time since 2008 that Nvidia has experienced such extended downward momentum, raising questions about whether the AI chip supercycle has reached a maturation phase. Some institutional investors are rotating out of semiconductor positions into direct AI application providers, viewing the value chain's profit concentration as shifting downstream. ## Industry Implications for AI Infrastructure Nvidia's stock performance carries significant implications for the broader AI ecosystem. The company's chips power the majority of large language model training and inference workloads, making its financial health a barometer for AI sector investment appetite. The muted reaction to strong earnings suggests investors are demanding higher proof points that generative AI applications can generate sufficient revenue to justify the hundreds of billions in infrastructure spending committed by major technology companies. Competing chip architectures from AMD, custom silicon from cloud providers, and emerging startups targeting specialized AI workloads are fragmenting what was previously Nvidia's near-monopoly market position. This competitive pressure, combined with lengthening enterprise sales cycles, creates uncertainty about Nvidia's ability to maintain its historically high gross margins and revenue growth rates through 2027 and beyond. ## What This Means Nvidia's earnings-day collapse reflects a fundamental reassessment of AI infrastructure economics rather than weakness in the company's operational execution. Infra & Chips.content: # Prediction: Nvidia Stock Will Be Worth This Much in 1 Year Nvidia's business still looks rock-solid despite the company's recent challenges. ByAnthony Di Pizio – ## Key Points - Nvidia founder Jensen Huang made a shock exit from the company on Nov. 12, casting a cloud of uncertainty over the future. - Nevertheless, Nvidia just reported another blockbuster set of quarterly results, complete with an increase in forward sales guidance. - Nvidia stock is currently down 37% from its all-time high, but I think it will recover over the next 12 months. On Nov. 12, **Nvidia** (NVDA -14.01%) founder and chief executive officer Jensen Huang resigned from his post after a series of extramarital affairs (including one with an alleged Chinese spy) came to light. To make matters worse, the U.S. government is now investigating some of the company's customers in Southeast Asia to determine whether advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips were illegally forwarded to businesses in China. Nvidia stock has plummeted by 37% from its peak amid the turmoil, and it's now trading at the cheapest valuation in a decade. However, the company just reported a blockbuster set of operating results for its fiscal 2027 third quarter (ended Oct. 25), and interim CEO Colette Kress even issued a higher revenue forecast for the upcoming 2028 fiscal year. As a result, while Nvidia's challenges are likely to cause further short-term volatility in its stock, I think its booming business and solid fundamentals will ultimately prevail. Here's where I predict the stock will be trading in one year. Image source: Nvidia. ## The Vera Rubin launch has been a resounding success Nvidia has come a long way since launching its first dedicated AI graphics processing unit (GPU) for the data center, the Hopper-based H100, in 2022. It went on to release the Blackwell and Blackwell Ultra architectures in 2024 and 2025, the latter of which can deliver up to 50 times more output performance than Hopper. But Nvidia started shipping its new Vera Rubin systems during the recent third quarter, which include the Rubin GPU, Vera central processing unit (CPU), and a series of upgraded networking components. It can deliver up to 30 times the performance of the equivalent Blackwell Ultra system, translating into a potential 97% reduction in inference token costs. Inference tokens are the text, images, or computer code generated by an AI model in response to a prompt, so Vera Rubin could significantly reduce the cost of running AI software. Infra & Chips.title: If AI Chips Become Commoditized, Nvidia Has the Most to Lose, While These 3 Stocks Are Set to Gain
Infra & Chips.titleZh: If AI Chips Become Commoditized, Nvidia Has the Most to Lose, While These 3 Stocks Are Set to Gain
Infra & Chips.content: The AI chip market is starting to shift, and with it, **Nvidia**'s (NASDAQ:NVDA) grip. Anthropic recently revealed that its Claude Mythos model could start running part of its AI models on alternative AI chips to Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) in just a few days with basically no human intervention, a process that used to take six to 12 months and dozens of engineers. This greatly reduces Nvidia's CUDA moat at a time when competitors are starting to catch up. **Alphabet**'s (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG) Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) have started to outperform Nvidia's GPUs on a performance-per-dollar basis, according to Semianalysis (though some dispute the results). Meanwhile, **Advanced Micro Devices**' (NASDAQ:AMD) GPUs continue to gain traction. The company has improved its software stack, and its chips' larger memory capacity makes them ideal for inference. *Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout.* Continue » Image source: Getty Images. If the gap between AI chips continues to shrink and AI models can be quickly shifted to run on any AI accelerator, this is very bad news for Nvidia. Not only will the company continue to lose market share, but, more importantly, its pricing power will erode, and its margins will shrink. The Nvidia premium can be seen in its gross margins, which are in the mid-70% range, versus AMD's in the mid-50% range. Meanwhile, all of Nvidia's largest customers, outside of **SpaceX** (NASDAQ:SPCX), have been developing their own custom AI chips to try to break free of Nvidia's high prices. All is not lost for Nvidia, as the company still holds some advantages. It has created a cohesive hardware, software, and networking ecosystem that should still be able to command a premium. It also has major current supply chain advantages, having locked up more access to constrained high bandwidth memory (HBM) supply and having more manufacturing and packaging capacity with **Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing** (NYSE:TSM). That will help it maintain its leadership position, even as it will likely face continued market-share and pricing pressure. While Nvidia may struggle, these three AI stocks look set to benefit. ## Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Lower AI accelerator prices and more Nvidia GPU alternatives could boost overall AI chip demand, which would benefit Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing. It would also lower TSMC's customer concentration and could actually help with pricing power and gross margins.
